title: Onboarding anti-entropy plan: live-drift decision tree & rollback playbook
author: Priya Nair
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines an anti-entropy onboarding strategy for new model variants and quantized artifacts. It prescribes a deterministic decision tree for detecting live drift, scoring signal fusion across quality/latency/cost telemetry, and executing automated or manual rollback paths. The goal is to ensure safe, observable promotions with clear thresholds and handoffs into regression triage.

Scope:
- Applies to: hosted, dedicated, and private deployments when promoting a model or quantized artifact from shadow to warm canary or prod.
- Includes: prompt families, function-call services, streaming sessions and embedding production indices.
- Excludes: offline-only evaluation artifacts and exploratory research snapshots.

Definitions:
- Entropy event: sudden increase in metric variance (quality, distribution, latency) vs. baseline.
- Signal fusion: combined score from weighted telemetry (quality, latency, token-cost, user-visible errors).
- Drift window: 30-minute rolling window used for early-detection gating.

Signals and thresholds (operational table):
| Signal | Aggregation | Normal baseline | Alert threshold | Escalation threshold | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Prompt-set fidelity (slice-level) | weighted F1/anchor score | >= 0.92 | drop >= 0.06 relative | drop >= 0.12 relative | compute per-priming-family |
| End-to-end latency P95 | rolling 30m P95 | <= 240ms | increase +40% | increase +80% or >1000ms | includes network and runtime |
| Token cost per request | mean over 30m | stable within 10% | increase +25% | increase +50% | signals quant fallback/bug |
| Function-call failure rate | calls per 30m | <= 0.5% | >= 1.5% | >= 5% | includes parse/format errors |
| Embedding drift (cosine) | average top-k sim delta | <= 0.04 | >= 0.08 | >= 0.16 | per-index and per-tenant |

Decision tree (short form):
1) Shadow comparison: run candidate under shadow for 24h (or smaller block for high-impact changes) with anchored probe families and production sampling.
2) Compute signal fusion score every 5 minutes: normalized signals weighted as {fidelity:0.45, latency:0.25, errors:0.15, cost:0.15}.
3) If fusion score breaches Alert threshold => auto-scale back to warm canary and create incident ticket with triage tag 'anti-entropy/alert'.
4) If fusion score breaches Escalation threshold or any single signal crosses Escalation threshold => automated rollforward block and execute rollback policy (see Rollback matrix).
5) If rolling windows recover for 2 consecutive evaluation windows (30m each) and human reviewer confirms, allow controlled rollforward (canary -> prod) with reduced weight.

Rollout phases and guardrails:
- Phase 0: Preflight (dev/test)
  - Unit tests, eval harness smoke, quant-compatibility sanity run.
  - Confirm quant profile and kernel availability.
- Phase 1: Shadow (0% traffic) for 24h or 10k sampled requests.
  - Collect anchored probe coverage and runtime fingerprint.
- Phase 2: Warm canary (1%–5% traffic) for 2–12h depending on impact score.
  - Gates: no fidelity drop > Alert threshold, P95 latency within limit, functional correctness tests green.
- Phase 3: Progressive ramp (5%->25%->100%) with automated checks at each step.

Rollback matrix (automated actions):
| Triggering condition | Immediate automated action | Human notify | Recovery step |
|---|---|---|---|
| Single-signal Escalation (e.g., P95 > 1000ms) | Quarantine traffic to fallback variant; freeze rollout | page oncall + owners | Roll back to last-succeeded artifact and trigger postmortem |
| Fusion Escalation | Abort promotion; mark artifact as unstable | page SRE + ML owner | Revert model, open regression triage board with sample set |
| Function-call spike > 5% | Disable streaming-to-function path for canary users | notify product + integrator | Route calls to preexisting stable variant |

Automated gating rules (implementation notes):
- Gate evaluation runs are implemented as a stateless service that consumes probe and production telemetry; every 5m it emits a 'gate' verdict (pass/warn/fail) with a scoring vector.
- Gate verdicts are deterministic and stored as immutable events for audit.
- For quantized artifacts, include a quant-compatibility check that runs 500 synthetic priming probes (slice-aware) before warm canary. Failures in >2% probes fail the gate.

Manual escalation playbook (when to escalate):
1) If gate verdict = fail for two consecutive windows OR any Escalation single-signal triggers -> create short incident channel with tags: model-name, artifact-id, canary-id, primary-signal, related-probes.
2) Tag the incident with "regression-hypothesis" and attach 3 representative probe payloads (highest divergence and highest user-frequency).
3) Triage owner assigns to regression team within 30 minutes. If unassigned, oncall SRE takes ownership.

Telemetry & alerts configuration (examples):
- Alert rule example (Prometheus-style):
  alert: ModelOnboardLatencyAlert
  expr: increase(model_request_duration_seconds_bucket{model="candidate"}[30m]) > 0.4
  for: 10m
  labels: {severity:critical, team:ml-serving}
- Fusion scorer settings (YAML example snippet):
  fusion_weights: 
    fidelity: 0.45
    latency: 0.25
    errors: 0.15
    cost: 0.15
  eval_window_mins: 30
  verdict_emit_interval_mins: 5

Ownership and runbook links:
- Model onboarding owner: ML Platform (team: runtime-onboarding). Primary contact: Priya Nair.
- Regression triage: Applied ML (team: model-regress).
- Runbooks: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/model-onboard-rollback-runbook-2025.json

Post-incident: triage and learnings checklist:
- Preserve full request/response traces and probe artifacts in tier-2 bucket for 90 days.
- Run automated bisect tool to test quant vs float behavior on anchored probes.
- Produce 'entropy report' summarizing which slices drove the decision (top-5) and suggested mitigations (prompt rewrite, quant-profile relax, prompt-family fallback).

Operational examples and CLI snippets:
- Promote candidate (safe-mode):
  rdi promote --model candidate-v2 --mode warm-canary --max-traffic 0.02 --guard-config=anti-entropy:v1
- Abort canary and revert:
  rdi rollback --canary-id canary-1234 --reason "fusion-escalation" --notify=oncall@redwood.com
- Export top probe failures:
  rdi probes export --artifact candidate-v2 --top 50 --out /tmp/failures.json

FAQ:
Q: How long should shadow runs be for low-traffic services?
A: For low-traffic services (<1k requests/day) use synthetic probe augmentation to reach 10k effective samples or extend shadow to 72h.

Q: When is quant-induced degradation expected?
A: Usually at priming-sensitive prompt families and long-context KV-cache heavy flows. The anti-entropy gate enforces a 2% synthetic-probe failure ceiling before any warm canary.

Appendix: sample gating YAML (single-file):
| key | value |
|---|---|
| fusion_weights | fidelity:0.45,latency:0.25,errors:0.15,cost:0.15 |
| eval_window_mins | 30 |
| probe_sample_count_for_quant | 500 |

Notes and rationale:
- Weighting fidelity highest reflects production-first commitment to customer-visible correctness.
- Rolling windows and dual-window recovery protect against transient flapping.
- Immutable gate verdicts and required probe attachments accelerate regression hunting.

Contact and feedback:
- Document owner: Priya Nair (priay@redwood.com). For edits, submit a PR to the onboarding playbook repo or ping #ml-onboard in Slack.
